source.title: NeuronFuzz: Safety Neuron Guided Fuzzing for LLM Safety Evaluation
source.authors: Zhiyuan Xu; Muhammad Firhard Roslan; Joseph Gardiner; Sana Belguith; Li-Chao Wu

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses selected safety-neuron activations as feedback for a jailbreak-fuzzing tool. Its results evaluate the oracle and fuzzing system, not whether neurons have one or a few human-nameable jobs or whether explanations predict activations on held-out examples.
record.gate_note: The paper measures how a classifier built from selected safety-neuron activations distinguishes harmful from benign prompts and how its score relates to jailbreak success. It does not audit neuron poles for semantic jobs, test explanations on activations they were not written from, evaluate attribution graphs, or report automated explanation scores. Fuzzing discovery and defense results compare the paper's method and are not results about the claim's neuron-level assertions. Results cited from prior work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The paper uses selected MLP neuron activations as features for a trained Elastic Net probe (SafetyOracle) that guides jailbreak fuzzing. It reports the probe's classification and its correlation with jailbreak success. It never examines whether individual neurons have one nameable job, never scores explanations against activations, and builds no attribution graphs. None of V1–V7 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that internal safety-neuron signals give continuous, prefill-only feedback that improves jailbreak discovery and transfers across models and modalities. They add that the SafetyOracle can also serve as an input-side detector of likely successful jailbreaks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses template-invariant activation extraction, stability-based feature selection, and a trained Elastic Net SafetyOracle to guide fuzzing; it does not use the claim's neuron-pole audit or explanation-testing procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that template-invariant extraction and stability-aware neuron selection affect oracle/fuzzing performance; its probe-model ablation also reports differing score-to-ASR correlations. These are method-component sensitivities, not changes in neuron interpretability shares.

fits_no_version.finding: On five source models, an Elastic Net probe over a stability-selected set of MLP gate/up activations separates harmful from benign clean prompts (AUROC 0.969–0.999). Its score drops under jailbreak templates and is lower for successful jailbreaks (Spearman −0.927 to −0.976 across score intervals).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A linear probe on a selected subset of MLP neurons carries a harmful-intent signal that tracks jailbreak susceptibility; this is a population-level readout, not a single-neuron job.

record.problems: The oracle findings are limited to the paper's selected safety-neuron features, trained scoring head, and stated prompt sets; they do not establish semantic interpretability of individual neurons. Some main table values have no uncertainty reported. The text reports 16 models in the setup and describes evaluations across 21 text and multimodal models, but that breadth does not test the listed neuron-interpretability versions.
record.rows_left_out: Fuzzing discovery, response-generation, time, transfer, defense, and detector results are not included because they evaluate the paper's new fuzzing or defense system rather than neuron-job interpretability or explanation prediction. The selection, fuzzing, and probe-model ablations are likewise method-component comparisons, not tests of the listed versions.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or job shares.
No neuron-job shares across models or scale. The paper covers dense and MoE models, but only for probe and fuzzing performance.
No vision models; no polysemantic-neuron reanalysis.
No interpretable-neuron shares versus architecture or tools.
No attribution graphs or circuit analysis.
No explanations of individual neurons tested against where they fire.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to none. The 'safety neurons' are features chosen by bootstrap stability selection and combined in a trained probe; the study makes no interpretability claim about individual neurons. Ablation Table 7 (random neurons AUROC 0.682 vs selected 0.989) is also a method comparison, not a test of any version.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or estimates of single-job, two-job, or not-understood shares.
No comparison of neuron-job shares across models, architectures, or scale.
No test or analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
No analysis of neuron interpretability shares in vision models or the effects of architecture, regularization, or tools on those shares.
No attribution graphs or test of whether model-own-neuron graphs explain behavior without a trained replacement model and its reconstruction error.
No evaluation of explanations fitted to activating examples against where a neuron fires.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by predicting activations on new text.
